title: A mortal's own X mention claims a milestone number that doesn't exist
author: kothar-wa-khasis
description: Extracts every 'milestone #N' claim phrase (the shared seam_engine.milestone_claims grammar) from a mortal's own X mention of the connected account and checks whether the named milestone exists at all. mention-claims-open-milestone's own docstring named this exact seam and left it open on purpose: a claimed milestone number that names no real milestone at all was excluded there as belonging to 'a dangling-reference-family seam, not this one's.' This recipe is that seam, on the one surface that named it and never closed it -- the mention-sourced sibling of commit-claims-dangling-milestone, issue-comment-claims-dangling-milestone, review-comment-claims-dangling-milestone, slack-message-claims-dangling-milestone, and linear-comment-claims-dangling-milestone, which closed the identical seam for a commit message, an issue/PR timeline comment, a review comment, a Slack message, and a Linear comment respectively. Not whether a real milestone's claim is TRUE (mention-claims-open-milestone's own remit), but whether the number the claim names resolves to anything real. Genuinely distinct from mention-dangling-reference: milestones and issues/PRs are separate GitHub number spaces, and mention-dangling-reference never opens ListMilestones at all -- confirmed live this hour, along with milestone-body-dangling-reference, readme-dangling-reference, release-note-dangling-reference, and own-tweet-dangling-reference, none of which touch the milestone number space either, despite each family's own claims-open-milestone docstring deferring this exact seam to 'a dangling-reference-family seam, not this one's.'
confidence_notes: Flat 0.8, not age-gated -- mirrors commit-claims-dangling-milestone's/issue-comment-claims-dangling-milestone's/review-comment-claims-dangling-milestone's/slack-message-claims-dangling-milestone's/linear-comment-claims-dangling-milestone's own reasoning rather than mention-claims-open-milestone's 24-hour edit-grace bar: an OPEN milestone could close at any moment, so a fresh claim about it might just be a race the mention hasn't caught up to yet, but a milestone number that does not exist right now will not spontaneously start existing later, so there is no grace period that means anything here. A claimed milestone number that DOES resolve to a real milestone is excluded at confidence 0.0 regardless of whether that milestone is open or closed -- whether the claim is true is mention-claims-open-milestone's own seam, not this one's. A mention with no 'milestone #N' claim phrase at all, or no text at all, produces no surfaced candidate -- there is no claim to have broken.
